title: The Cautious Tale of Cal AI: luck, headhunters, and hiring for availability and learning
summary: Jake Castillo says Cal AI's rise to #1 in Health & Fitness and $50M ARR in eighteen months owed a lot to luck, not a replicable process. His practical advice: pay for great talent via headhunters, sell candidates hard, give generous equity, and hire for availability and ability to learn over experience.

principles.text: Luck plays a big role in winning; hard work and smarts mainly increase your surface area for luck.
principles.quote: Working hard and being smart just increases your surface area for luck.

principles.text: Don't wait to assemble a perfect, once-in-a-lifetime founding team; you may die waiting.
principles.quote: So if you are sitting there waiting to assemble a group of once-in-a-lifetime, Avengers style co-founders who happen to be brilliant AND happen to get along AND happen to be available, you might die waiting.

principles.text: Great talent is expensive and has options, so you have to pay to play.
principles.quote: Great people are expensive, hard to find, and already have options.

principles.text: Use a headhunter (about 20% of first-year salary) to source top talent fast; most founders are bad at sourcing.
principles.quote: Their fees usually cost around 20% of first-year salary and it is 100% worth it, because sourcing great talent is mind-numbing work and most founders have not hired enough people to be any good at it.

principles.text: Sell strong candidates hard on joining, since the best people don't need you, and be generous with equity.
principles.quote: you have to sell them hard on why they should work with you, because the person you want does not usually need you.

principles.text: Hire for availability and ability to learn rather than experience alone; experience can work against you.
principles.quote: Is this person actually here, and can they figure out something they do not currently know?
